answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the voyage fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the vault ledger attributes every share, the relic audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 71% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not burn. That is 9 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
